 Flu visits at Whatcom emergency room at 6-year high
 Month into flu season, Whatcom County has already seen a flu-related death
 Oct. 30, 2026 1:38 p.m. 
 By 
 Owen Racer 
 Healthcare/Public Health Reporter 
 No Q&A content found.
 Whatcom County is experiencing an abnormally high rate of flu hospitalizations to start this respiratory illness season. The rate of emergency department visits in Whatcom County with positive flu tests is higher this October than the previous six years, according to Whatcom County Health and Community Services.
 October has historically been the beginning of flu season; there has already been one flu-related death in Whatcom County this year, according to the health department. Last year, the county saw two flu-related deaths. The year prior, there were 17.
 Whatcom County’s emergency department is seeing flu rates not typically seen until December.
 The county health department recommends flu vaccines as the best protection. Minors and individuals without insurance can receive free childhood vaccines and some adult vaccines at county-provided immunization clinics .
